## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Somanassa Sutta* (Iti 37) is a short discourse in the *Dukanipāta* (Book of the Twos) of the *Itivuttaka* (PTS It 29–30) [SuttaCentral; Piya Tan 2004]. Its central theme is religious urgency (*saṁvega*) and its practical fruits: the text teaches that when endowed with two qualities—a keen sense of urgency and appropriate exertion—a monastic dwells in great mental ease and happiness in the present life (*diṭṭhe va dhamme somanassavihārī*) while wisely rousing effort toward the destruction of the mental defilements or influxes (*āsavānaṁ khayāya*) [SuttaCentral; Piya Tan 2004].
